title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog: exploitation-prioritized remediation rail
summary: CISA KEV is encoded as a prioritization rail: it distinguishes vulnerabilities known to be exploited in the wild from the much larger public-vulnerability universe. The record does not treat KEV as a full software-failure archive or as a postmortem substitute.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0010 as vulnerability/source-infrastructure rail for the software failure lane.

claims.claim: CISA’s official source-index describes the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog as an authoritative source of vulnerabilities exploited in the wild and an input to vulnerability-prioritization decisions.
what_would_change_status: An accessible CISA archive/API source changes the stated KEV purpose or authoritative-source language.

evidence_refs.locator: CISA KEV official search result / dynamic page source-index

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: CISA’s BOD 22-01 official source-index says it establishes a managed catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities carrying significant risk to the federal enterprise; NVD also states that it prioritizes CVEs in the CISA KEV catalog for enrichment.
what_would_change_status: CISA changes BOD/KEV requirements or NVD changes the KEV-prioritization note.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official/institutional source extraction; no coverage or outcome audit
limitations: Establishes infrastructure existence and declared function only.
Does not claim completeness, timeliness, exploit prevalence, patch compliance, or incident-prevention effect.

outputs: required action dates for federal context where applicable

does not prove individual asset compromise

type_payload.query_value: Lets the cube distinguish ordinary known vulnerabilities from those already seen in exploitation while preserving non-equivalence with postmortem and failure-investigation records.

handling_notes: Vulnerability infrastructure records should not become exploit catalogues; keep to identifier, enrichment, prioritization, and remediation-governance roles.
Do not infer patch status, exploitation, or blame from mere presence/absence in a vulnerability catalog without record-specific evidence.

unknowns: Coverage, timeliness, enrichment lag, and real remediation effects are not audited.
Dynamic/403/source-index pages need archive/API pass where relevant.
next_actions: Sample records to test identifier-to-patch-to-incident linkage.
Create negative-control cases where vulnerability rails worked and incidents were averted.
